thread.title: Home Is Where the Heart Is? Apple Is Ready To Splurge in U.S. After Repatriation Tax

author: Jon Swartz
title: Home Is Where the Heart Is? Apple Is Ready To Splurge in U.S. After Repatriation Tax
text:
(Photo by Justin Sullivan/Getty Images) Illustration: Justin Sullivan/Getty Images Amazon ( AMZN ) isn't the only tech behemoth planning a second major U.S. campus .
Apple ( AAPL ) on Wednesday said it will announce another campus later this year as part of a 5-year, $30 billion U.S. investment program.
The Cupertino, Calif.-based company intends to create 20,000 jobs through its new campus and its existing headquarters. It's also expected to spend big on data centers to house its iCloud , App Store and Apple Music services.
Apple said it will also pay $38 billion in taxes on its cash overseas.
The mammoth tax payment is roughly in line with what analysts anticipated from the recently passed national tax bill, which requires companies to pay a one-time tax on foreign-held earnings, regardless of where the money is stashed. Apple, which has $252.3 billion in cash overseas, did not indicate how much -- if any -- of its cash hoard it would bring back to the U.S.
"Apple, already the largest U.S. taxpayer, anticipates repatriation tax payments of approximately $38 billion as required by recent changes to the tax law," the company said in a statement. "A payment of that size would likely be the largest of its kind ever made."
Separately, Apple told employees on Wednesday it's rewarding them $2,500 in restricted stock units as a result of the new U.S. tax law, according to a report in Bloomberg , citing people familiar with the matter.
Amazon, based in Seattle, completed taking applications from cities in October for its second campus.
